files.why: DTOs are the server-shape contract; rename the zod schema keys and add the extra nesting level for line items here — the API change lands in data/ by design.
The DTO<->core mapper must read the renamed fields and reach one level deeper for line items so core entities stay unchanged — this is where the mapper 'earns its keep'.
MSW seed data is authored in server shape, so the fixtures must adopt the renamed fields and the deeper line-item nesting to match the new API.
Its hard-coded InvoiceDto literal and round-trip expectations encode the old field names/flat lines and would fail; update them to the new server shape.

uncertain: apps/web/src/slices/billing/data/queries.ts and mutations.ts: likely NO change, since they consume invoiceDtoSchema/toInvoice by their existing names. They'd only need touching if the schema/type export names themselves change or if the deeper nesting requires a different parse call — unsure without the exact new shape.

Whether core/ (types.ts, rules.ts, policy.ts) and ui/ stay untouched. The architecture's premise is that a pure wire-format change is fully absorbed by data/. I'm treating this as wire-only; if the backend change also reflects a genuine domain-model change, core/ and its tests (billing.core.test.ts) would also move — but nothing in the request implies that.
